description: Public edition: Networks of brain-inspired computing devices designed for specialized low-power perception and processing tasks.
body:
Neuromorphic Civilization Computing. Networks of brain-inspired computing devices designed for specialized low-power perception and processing tasks.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 64 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Computing Beyond the Conventional Computer". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Neuromorphic chips (TrueNorth 2014, Loihi 2017/2021) are real; civilization-scale deployment is unproven.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Neuromorphic Civilization Computing - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Networks of brain-inspired computing devices designed for specialized low-power perception and processing tasks.
body:
Known science foundations of Neuromorphic Civilization Computing.

IBM TrueNorth (1M neurons) and Intel Loihi/Loihi 2 demonstrate event-driven low-power computing. BrainScaleS and SpiNNaker explore large-scale neural simulation. Applications in sensing and robotics show power advantages. Programming models and benchmarks lag; no killer app at scale yet.

Key quantity check (Loihi 2 neurons / human cortical neurons): computed ratio 6.25e-05 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.3. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Neuromorphic Civilization Computing - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Networks of brain-inspired computing devices designed for specialized low-power perception and processing tasks.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Neuromorphic Civilization Computing.

Programming neuromorphic hardware is difficult. Benchmarks vs GPUs are contested. Device variability complicates deployment.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 22.2 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is brain neurons vs energy per spike at 22.2 orders of magnitude (brain neurons larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Neuromorphic Civilization Computing - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: Networks of brain-inspired computing devices designed for specialized low-power perception and processing tasks.
body:
Unresolved problems for Neuromorphic Civilization Computing, in priority order (research burden index 15, 1 blocking):

A decisive application advantage (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Usable programming models (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

Manufacturing at scale (severity 2/3, tractability 3/3; priority 2).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
